docs.title: Tree Carve
docs.text:
Cut a message into a tree. Hit a log with a sword and type what you want on it — a name, a warning, a heart — and it stays there, cut into the bark, for anyone who walks past.

It registers no items and adds no recipes. The tool is the sword you already carry, and the only ways to lose a message are an axe and losing the log it is on.

MC 1.21.1 MC 26.1–26.3 Fabric NeoForge No Cobblemon

Get started

docs.title: What can it do?
docs.text:
• Carve with a sword — sneak + right-click any log, of any wood, vanilla or modded. The face is a canvas: text and symbols you move, size and turn.
  • Seventeen symbols, five typefaces — hearts, stars, an aiaigasa, a skull and more, each a piece of its own. The Pokeball turns up when Cobblemon is installed.
  • In colour — the dyes you are carrying tint the cut. The log keeps its own bark, and the lettering takes the shade of that species' own stripped wood.
  • An axe takes it off — stripping a carved log strips it exactly as vanilla does, and the message goes with the bark.
  • Built for servers — only the author or an operator can rewrite a carving, @ mentions, a blocked-words list, and commands to find and remove any player's carvings.
  • Bring your own symbols — a datapack adds symbols and typefaces to the pickers, and a resource pack can bring artwork that takes the tone of every wood.

docs.title: The one rule
docs.text: A message belongs to the log it is cut into. Fell the tree and the message is gone with it; build something else on that spot and whatever was there is cleared. Nothing survives the block it was written on, which is why a carving is worth walking to.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Download Modrinth · What changed Version 2.0.0 Minecraft 1.21.1 · 26.1–26.3 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon Not needed Fabric Architectury API, Fabric Language Kotlin NeoForge Architectury API, Kotlin for Forge Java 21 for Minecraft 1.21.1, 25 for 26.x Works with any mod that adds logs — it goes by the block tag, not by a list of woods

Each Minecraft version has its own jar, and the file name ends in it (tree-carve-fabric-2.0.0+26.3.jar). Drop the one for your Minecraft version and loader into mods/, never both loaders at once. New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Install the jar for your Minecraft version and loader, along with its dependencies. There is nothing to craft and nothing to unlock: the tool is the sword you already carry.

docs.title: Carving
docs.text:
Sneak + right-click a log with a sword. Any sword, including one from another mod, and any log, including one from another mod. The carving screen opens on the face you clicked.

A plain left-click with the sword chops the log exactly as it always did; only the sneaking right-click carves.

Out of the box, a log that is already stripped cannot be carved: an axe could not take the message off it again. A server can change which blocks take a carving.

Opening the screen is free. Writing a message costs 1 durability from the sword and plays a carving sound; close the screen without changing anything and nothing is spent. A server may change the cost.

docs.title: The carving screen
docs.text:
The face is a canvas. You build a carving out of pieces, text and symbols, and arrange them on it however you like.

To Do Add a piece Add text or Add symbol Move a piece Drag it Resize it Drag its corner handle Rotate it Drag the arm above it; hold Shift to snap to 15° steps. Or use ↺, 0° and ↻ Remove it Select it and press Delete, or the Delete button Finish Enter (when you are not typing in a text box), or the screen's confirm button

One face holds up to 16 pieces and 240 characters of text across all of them. A server may change both limits.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Each text piece has its own style and font:

  • B, I, U and S turn on bold, italic, underline and strikethrough, in any combination.
  • The Font picker offers Carved, the default, and four more: Plain, Unifont, Galactic and Illager runes. A datapack can add more; see Custom Symbols & Fonts.

Type @ at the start of a word to pick a name from everyone who has ever joined the server.

docs.title: Symbols
docs.text:
A symbol is a piece of its own, placed, sized and turned like text. Seventeen ship with the mod:

Heart · Hollow heart · Umbrella · Aiaigasa · Skull · Star · Hollow star · Flower · Music note · Sun · Cloud · Snowflake · Anchor · Crown · Arrow · Cross · Pokeball

The Pokeball appears only when Cobblemon is installed. Text laid over a symbol is cut into it.

docs.title: Colour
docs.text: The Colour picker offers the dyes you are carrying, any of the sixteen. The dye tints the wood rather than painting over it, so a red carving in oak still reads as oak. The dye is spent when you confirm. Re-saving a carving whose colours have not changed costs no dye.

docs.title: Editing and ownership
docs.text:
Sneak + right-click a face that already carries a message and the screen opens with that carving in it, ready to change. Removing every piece and confirming deletes the carving.

Only the person who cut a carving, or an operator, can rewrite it. Anyone else sees "Somebody else carved this. An axe takes it off." A server can let anyone edit; see Server Admin.

docs.title: What it looks like
docs.text: The bark is not repainted. A carved log looks like the log it is, and the lettering reads as fresh-cut timber, in a shade taken from that species' own stripped wood, with a shadowed groove under every cut. An oak carving and a warped stem carving look like their own trees rather than the same paint on two backgrounds. Carvings are drawn from up to 48 blocks away.

docs.title: Removing a carving
docs.text:
Strip the log with an axe. It strips exactly as vanilla does and the message goes with the bark. This works on anyone's carving, not only your own.

Stripping converts the whole block, not the face you were pointing at, so every message on that log is gone, not only the one in front of you. An axe on a log with nothing carved on it behaves as it always has.

docs.title: What a carving does not survive
docs.text:
• Breaking the log. Fell the tree and the message goes with it.
  • Building over the spot. Whatever was there is cleared with the block.

There is no way to move a carving, and nothing keeps one alive past the block it was cut into.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: • A world moved from Minecraft 1.21.1 to 26.x does not bring its carvings along. 26.x keeps them in a file with a different name and does not read the old one. A world started on 26.x keeps its carvings like any other.

docs.title: Server Admin
docs.text: Everything here needs operator level 2.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Command What it does /treecarve config Lists every setting with its value and range. /treecarve config <key> Shows one setting. /treecarve config <key> <value> Changes one setting. /treecarve config reset Puts every setting back to its default. reset <key> does one. /treecarve reload Re-reads the file after you edited it by hand.

Settings are saved to config/tree_carve.json. If the file cannot be read, it is left untouched and the server runs on the defaults until you fix it and run /treecarve reload.

docs.title: What can be carved
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning carving true Whether a sword carves anything at all. carveOnStripped false Stripped logs can be carved. carveOnPlanks false Planks can be carved. carveOnAnyWood false Anything an axe mines can be carved. axeStrips true Stripping a carved log with an axe takes the message with the bark. allowEditOthers false Anyone may rewrite a carving somebody else cut. Off, only the author and operators can. An axe removes any carving either way.

Some of these cannot be undone with an axe

A message cut into a stripped log, a plank or other wood comes off only by breaking the block: there is no bark left to strip. The same goes for every carving when axeStrips is false. Turn these on knowing that the only remover left is a pickaxe, an axe swing that breaks the block, or /treecarve remove.

docs.title: Limits and cost
docs.text:
Key Default Range Meaning swordDurability 1 0–64 Durability the sword loses per message written. maxElements 16 1–64 Pieces one face may hold. maxTotalChars 240 1–240 Characters across every text piece on a face. allowDye true A piece can be carved in colour with a dye the player is carrying. consumeDye true Spend the dye. Off, it only has to be in the inventory. carveSound true Play a sound at the log when a message is written.

maxElements, maxTotalChars and blockedWords apply to the next carving; what is already cut is left alone.

docs.title: Look
docs.text: Key Default Range Meaning letterLighten 42 0–100 How far toward white the lettering is pushed, in percent. grooveDarken 25 0–100 How dark the inside of the cut is, in percent. dyeStrength 65 0–100 How far the wood is pulled toward the dye, in percent. renderDistance 48 8–128 How far away a carving is drawn, in blocks. surfaceOffset 3 1–50 How far the lettering sits off the bark, in thousandths of a block. Raise it if a black mesh flickers.

docs.title: Datapack tables
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning datapackSymbols true Load symbols from datapacks. datapackFonts true Load fonts from datapacks.

Both need a /reload to take effect. What they switch off is explained in Custom Symbols & Fonts.

docs.title: Moderation
docs.text:
Command What it does /treecarve who Who cut the face you are looking at, its text and how many symbols it holds. /treecarve remove Clears the face you are looking at. /treecarve list <player> Every carving by that player in every dimension, up to 50. Click a line to get the command that takes you there. /treecarve removeall <player> Clears every carving by that player, online or not.

Every removal is written to the server log with who did it and what the carving said. A carving made by a command or another mod has no author, and shows as nobody.

docs.title: Blocked words
docs.text:
/treecarve config blockedWords add "word"
/treecarve config blockedWords remove "word"

A blocked word is masked with asterisks wherever it stands as a whole word, in any case. The list exists because a carving never passes through chat, so a chat-filter mod never sees it. Quote a word with accents or spaces.

docs.title: Custom Symbols & Fonts
docs.text:
The symbol picker and the font picker are not lists baked into the mod. Each is a table loaded from datapacks, and the built-in hearts, stars and typefaces are ordinary entries in it. A pack can add its own symbol, its own artwork or its own typeface, override a built-in, or hide one behind another mod, with no code change.

This page is for pack authors and server owners. Players only need Getting Started.

docs.title: Two kinds of pack
docs.text:
Pack Ships Needed for Datapack data/<pack>/tree_carve/symbol/<name>.json and data/<pack>/tree_carve/font/<name>.json every entry — this is what puts it in the picker Resource pack a bitmap font and its PNG, plus a language file only when the entry draws artwork of its own, or when it needs a readable name

The datapack lives on the server and the tables are sent to every player on join and again after each /reload. The resource pack lives on each client: on a server, every player needs it (a server resource pack is the usual way), or they see the entry without its artwork.

docs.title: A symbol from a datapack alone
docs.text:
A symbol is one character of a font, not a picture. Minecraft already carries Unifont, which covers a great deal of Unicode — suits, weather, chess pieces, tools — so a datapack alone can offer any of those characters:

data/mypack/tree_carve/symbol/swords.json

{
  "glyph": "\u2694",
  "order": 25
}

That is a complete symbol: crossed swords, placed in the picker between the umbrellas and the skull. With no font, the glyph is drawn in the player's default font.

docs.title: A symbol with artwork of its own
docs.text: When Unicode has no character for what you want, ship a bitmap font in a resource pack and point a symbol at one of its glyphs. tree_carve:pokeball is built exactly this way and is in the mod's jar if you want a working copy to start from.

docs.title: Draw it white
docs.text:
The sheet must be white on transparent, or greyscale

A carving is tinted with the wood it is cut into. The mod draws every glyph in one colour taken from that species' stripped wood, and that colour multiplies every pixel of the glyph. A full-colour sheet comes out as your art times the timber, which reads as mud.

That is the feature, not a limitation: one white sheet comes out oak on an oak, birch on a birch and warped-green on a warped stem. Use grey for shading inside the shape.

docs.title: The resource pack: a bitmap font
docs.text:
assets/mypack/font/symbols.json

{
  "providers": [
    {
      "type": "bitmap",
      "file": "mypack:font/symbols.png",
      "ascent": 8,
      "height": 10,
      "chars": ["\ue000\ue001"]
    }
  ]
}

The PNG goes in assets/mypack/textures/font/symbols.png, one equal-sized cell per character in chars. Use code points from the Private Use Area (\ue000 onwards) so they never collide with real text. Draw the cells large — a symbol can be stretched across a whole trunk, and a bigger cell keeps its edges clean.

docs.title: The datapack: the symbol entry
docs.text:
data/mypack/tree_carve/symbol/lantern.json

{
  "glyph": "\ue000",
  "font": "mypack:symbols",
  "order": 75
}

docs.title: Symbol fields
docs.text:
Field Required Meaning glyph yes What is drawn. Usually one character; a short string is allowed. font no The font the glyph is looked up in, as <namespace>:<name>. Left out, the player's default font. order no Position in the picker, lowest first. Ties break on the symbol's id. Defaults to 0. requires_mod no A mod id. The symbol is offered only when that mod is loaded.

requires_mod gates the picker and nothing else. A trunk already carrying the symbol keeps showing it after that mod is removed — a carving is something a player made, and a changed mod list is not a reason to erase it. This is how the pokeball appears only with Cobblemon installed.

docs.title: Fonts
docs.text:
A font entry offers a typeface a message can be cut in. It names a font the client already has, vanilla's or one shipped in a resource pack:

data/mypack/tree_carve/font/runes.json

{
  "font": "mypack:runes",
  "order": 50
}
Field Required Meaning font yes The font, as <namespace>:<name> — a font JSON under assets/<namespace>/font/. order no Position in the picker, lowest first. Ties break on the id. Defaults to 0.

The same white-or-greyscale rule applies to a bitmap typeface: letters are tinted with the wood exactly as symbols are.

docs.title: Names in the picker
docs.text:
The picker shows a translated name for every entry, built from its id:

Entry Language key symbol mypack:lantern tree_carve.symbol.mypack.lantern font mypack:runes tree_carve.font.mypack.runes

Put them in your resource pack's assets/mypack/lang/en_us.json. Without one, the picker shows the raw key.

docs.title: Overriding and ordering
docs.text:
An entry with the same id as a built-in replaces it. To change the heart, ship data/tree_carve/tree_carve/symbol/heart.json in your datapack; a higher-priority datapack wins, as with any other datapack file.

To slot a new entry between two built-ins, pick an order between theirs.

Symbol Id Order Pokeball (Cobblemon only) tree_carve:pokeball 5 Heart tree_carve:heart 10 Hollow heart tree_carve:heart_outline 11 Umbrella tree_carve:umbrella 20 Aiaigasa tree_carve:aiaigasa 21 Skull tree_carve:skull 30 Star tree_carve:star 40 Hollow star tree_carve:star_outline 41 Flower tree_carve:flower 50 Music note tree_carve:note 60 Sun tree_carve:sun 70 Cloud tree_carve:cloud 71 Snowflake tree_carve:snowflake 72 Anchor tree_carve:anchor 80 Crown tree_carve:crown 90 Arrow tree_carve:arrow_right 100 Cross tree_carve:cross 110 Font Id Order Carved (the default) tree_carve:carved 0 Plain tree_carve:default 10 Unifont tree_carve:unifont 20 Galactic tree_carve:alt 30 Illager runes tree_carve:illageralt 40

docs.title: When a pack is removed
docs.text:
A carving stores the symbol's id, never its glyph. Uninstall the pack and its symbols stop drawing, but every trunk keeps the id; install the pack again and they come back as they were. Nothing is rewritten in the meantime.

A text piece whose font entry is gone is drawn in plain Minecraft text until the font returns, so the message stays readable.

A file that cannot be read — not a JSON object, a symbol without glyph, a font without font — is skipped and named in the server log. The rest of the table still loads.

docs.title: Switching the tables off
docs.text:
Two settings stop the tables from loading at all:

Setting Stops datapackSymbols every tree_carve/symbol file datapackFonts every tree_carve/font file

Set them with /treecarve config datapackSymbols false or /treecarve config datapackFonts false. The change takes effect on the next /reload.

Off means the table is empty, built-ins included — the built-ins are datapack files like any other. Carvings already on trunks keep their ids and draw again once the table is switched back on.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common surprises, what causes them, and what to do. If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: My carving disappeared
docs.text: A carving lives in the block it was cut into. Breaking the log, or building over the spot, takes it with the block, and an axe that strips the bark takes the message too (unless an operator turned axeStrips off). See What a carving does not survive.

docs.title: I cannot remove a carving with an axe
docs.text: A message on a stripped log, a plank or other wood has no bark left to strip, and neither does any carving when axeStrips is false. Break the block, or an operator can use /treecarve remove.

docs.title: My carvings are gone after moving the world to 26.x
docs.text: A world moved from Minecraft 1.21.1 to 26.x does not bring its carvings along: 26.x keeps them in a file with a different name and does not read the old one. A world started on 26.x keeps its carvings like any other.

docs.title: The wrong jar
docs.text: Each Minecraft version has its own jar, and its file name ends in that version (tree-carve-fabric-2.0.0+26.3.jar). Use the one for your Minecraft version and loader, never both loaders at once.

docs.title: My custom symbol sheet looks wrong
docs.text: The sheet must be white on transparent, or greyscale. See Custom Symbols & Fonts.
